summary: Repaired and applied the transactional SQLite v1-to-v2 upgrade on node1. The catalog remains healthy and persists across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Updated bin/upgrade.py for Python 2.4 and the legacy sqlite module.
Made schema and version changes atomic with rollback on failure.
Added price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (price_cents >= 0).
Restarted node1 and verified recovery with a changed boot identity.

evidence.requirement: Retain existing IDs and descriptions and initialize price_cents to zero
evidence.summary: Production database is version 2; products remain (1, Paper) and (2, Tape), both priced at zero.
Negative values are rejected by the CHECK constraint; post-restart verification found zero negative prices.

evidence.requirement: Advance schema_version only after the whole upgrade succeeds and preserve v1 on failure
evidence.summary: A forced failure during the version update rolled back the column addition, retaining version 1, original data, and database integrity.
The migration completed twice successfully in isolation and twice against production without duplicate changes.

evidence.requirement: Remain compatible with the installed legacy operating system and kernel
evidence.summary: Migration uses the installed Python 2.4/PySQLite stack; CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained unchanged.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 8ca45596-927a-495c-8000-000000000000, received restart acknowledgement, observed new boot ID 88f134c9-16a6-4625-8000-000000000000, and verified the version-2 catalog, retained data, repeat-safe migration, constraints, and integrity after recovery.
